back_translation: The burden-oracle concerning Damascus: Behold, Damascus will be removed from being a city and will become a heap of collapsed ruins.
The cities of Aroer will be abandoned; they will become a place for flocks, which will lie down with no one to make them afraid.
The fortress will vanish from Ephraim, and royal sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the sons of Israel — thus the LORD of Hosts has declared.
In that day the glory of Jacob will sink low, and the fatness of his flesh will waste away to leanness.
And it will be as when a reaper gathers the standing grain and his arm harvests the ears — as when someone gleans fallen ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

Yet leftover gleanings will remain in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives left at the very top bough, four or five on its fruitful branches — thus the LORD, the God of Israel, has declared.
In that day mankind will look to his Maker, and his eyes will gaze at the Holy One of Israel.
He will not look to the altars that are the work of his own hands, nor gaze at what his fingers have made — neither the Asherah poles nor the incense altars.
In that day their strong cities will be like the abandoned places of the thicket and the mountaintop, deserted before the sons of Israel; and all will become desolation.
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you plant delightful plants and set out vine-slips of a foreign vine,
though on the day you plant you make them flourish, and on the morning you sow you make them blossom — yet the harvest will vanish away in the day of disease, and the pain will be beyond healing.
Woe to the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the sea! Woe to the thundering of nations, who crash like the crashing of mighty waters!

The nations thunder like the rushing of many flooding waters; but He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away — chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind, like whirling dust before the storm.
At evening time, behold — sudden horror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who loot us.
